title: Technology Sector Update for 09/25/2018: IRDM,XOXO,CTL,JBL
text:

Technology stocks trimmed most of their prior declines, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 Tuesday losing less than 0.1% in value although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index continued its steep slide this afternon, sinking over 1.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Iridium ( IRDM ) rose over 6% on Tuesday, climbing to within 1% again of its all-time high of $21.55 a share, after a non-profit organization selected the satellite communications company to assist with its efforts to remove plastic debris from the Pacific Ocean. The Ocean Cleanup group has developed a network consisting of 60 floating plastic collectors, with each of the 600-meter-long collectors to be equipped with two Iridium broadband terminals and associated sensors to relay video and system performance data as well as positioning and location information to the Ocean Cleanup headquarters. Iridium Tuesday also said its replacement satellite constellation, Iridium Next, was now almost in place, needing only one more SpaceX launch to complete the low-earth orbit formation of 66 active L-band satellites and nine spares.
In other sector news:
(+) XO Group ( XOXO ) rose as much as 26% on Tuesday after the digital marketplace company agreed to a $933 million merger and going-private transaction led by private equity investors Permira Funds and Spectrum Equity. Under terms of the proposed buyout, XO Group investors will receive $35 in cash for each of their shares, representing a 27% premium to Monday's closing price. The operator of The Knot ecommerce web site also will be merged with WeddingWire, which like The Knot, targets wedding customers. The transaction is expected to close during the first half of 2019.
(-) CenturyLink ( CTL ) slipped nearly 9% on Tuesday after saying chief financial officer Sunit Patel will step down on Friday to accept an executive position at another company. The networking services company has named Neel Dev, currently its group vice president for finance, to assume Patel's former duties on an interim basis and will soon begin an internal and external search for a permanent finance chief.
(-) Jabil Circuit ( JBL ) retreated Tuesday, at one point falling over 10%, despite reporting core fiscal Q4 net income and revenue exceeding Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.70 per share, improving on a $0.64 per share core profit during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue rose to $5.77 billion from $5.02 billion last year and also topping the $5.41 billion analyst mean.
